newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania exports earnings decline but revenue up.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania exports earnings decline but revenue up.

text.p: Tanzanian export earnings fell 10.6 percent in June but annual inflation was down and revenue collection was up, the Bank of Tanzania (BoT) said on Thursday.

The BoT monthly report said year-to-year inflation dropped slightly from May's 16.5 percent to 16.4 percent in June. The central bank said the overall inflationary trend was down, with June inflation down from 22.7 percent in June 1996.
"The continuation of the downward trend of underlying inflation is an indication of the effectiveness of monetary and fiscal policies," it said.
Actual underlying inflation, the rate of inflation excluding food prices, fell three percent from 10.3 percent in May to 7.3 percent in June.
Tanzania's traditional exports, with the exception of coffee, decreased by 24.6 percent. Cotton, sisal, tea, tobacco and cashewnuts registered drops in export volume.
June trade account deficit was $76.7 million compared to $64.5 million in May, the bank said.

The trade deterioration was attributed to the 10.6-percent decrease in export earnings from $47.3 million in May to $42.3 million in June and a 24.3-percent increase in the import bill from $95.8 million in May to $119 million in June.
The import gains resulted from increases in all major categories. Capital goods, intermediate goods and consumer goods rose 9.8 percent, 68 percent and six percent, respectively.

The capital goods surge involved building and construction equipment and machinery, "an indication of an expansion in investment activities in both the construction and manufacturing sectors," the bank said.
Total external debt as of June 30 stood at $7.9 billion.
